```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
Q    <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/pumseq/pumseq_processed/psi_qtl/qtl_betabinomial"
OLD  <- file.path(Q, "pc_window_selection/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/summary")         # k = 3..15, 5-50 kb
NEW  <- file.path(Q, "pc_window_selection_w200kb/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/summary")  # k = 3, 5, 5-200 kb
NOM  <- file.path(Q, "nominal_wide_window/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/w2000kb_pc3/summary")
fmt  <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
pct  <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
th   <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

so <- fread(file.path(OLD, "selection_table.tsv")); sn <- fread(file.path(NEW, "selection_table.tsv"))
co <- fread(file.path(OLD, "selection_no_inheritedC.tsv")); cn <- fread(file.path(NEW, "selection_no_inheritedC.tsv"))
# k = 3 and 5 from the extended run (all five windows, deduplicated genotypes); k = 7, 10, 15 from the first run
ST <- rbind(sn[, src := "extended run"], so[!npcs %in% sn$npcs][, src := "first run"], fill = TRUE)
SC <- rbind(cn, co[!npcs %in% cn$npcs], fill = TRUE)
chk <- merge(sn[window_kb <= 50, .(window_kb, npcs, a = disc_q10)], so[, .(window_kb, npcs, b = disc_q10)], by = c("window_kb", "npcs"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk) > 0, all(chk$a == chk$b))   # the extended run reproduces the first one at 5-50 kb (q < 0.10)
G  <- fread(file.path(Q, "calibration_grid/grid_calibration.tsv"))
lam3 <- G[npcs == 3, sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(perm_lambda_min), max(perm_lambda_max))]
S  <- fread(file.path(NOM, "strong_pairs_p0.0001.tsv.gz"))[, absd := abs(dist_bp)]
EN <- fread(file.path(NOM, "enrichment_by_distance.tsv"))
FL <- fread(file.path(Q, "stage1_open_questions/farlead.tsv"))
e  <- function(k, w, v = "disc_q10") ST[npcs == k & window_kb == w, get(v)]
```

Stage 2 identifies **Ψ sites with at least one significant cis-QTL (eSites)**,
following the approach of the m6A-QTL study (Zhang et al. 2020).

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(data.table(
  item = c("test", "fitter", "covariates", "genotypes", "site significance", "FDR", "status"),
  value = c("beta-binomial likelihood-ratio test per SNP-site pair: logit(mean) = intercept + k PCs (+ genotype)",
            "maximum likelihood with three starting values of the overdispersion (a single start sometimes stopped at a false optimum)",
            "k phenotype PCs; k under review (section 2)",
            "8.54 M biallelic SNPs with MAF >= 0.05; duplicated variant IDs (hg19 -> hg38 liftover collisions) removed",
            "per-site permutations of phenotype and covariates together across cell lines; beta approximation; Storey q-values",
            "10%, as in the paper",
            "k under review (0-1 PCs give more eSites; calibration at k = 0/1 being checked); cis window pending; final scan (about 1,000 permutations) not yet run")),
  col.names = c("", ""))
```

# 1. Calling eSites

For each site, every cis SNP is tested and the smallest p-value is kept. The
phenotype and the covariates are then permuted together across the 50 cell lines
(genotypes fixed) and the scan is repeated; the minima of the permutations are
fitted with a beta distribution, which turns the site's smallest p-value into a
permutation p-value that accounts for the number of SNPs tested. Storey q-values
across sites give the eSites (q < 0.10). The scans below use 100 permutations per
site; the final scan will use more.

At k = 3 the permutations are well calibrated in bulk (genomic-control lambda of
permuted data `r lam3`); the same check at k = 0 and 1 is running. QQ plots for every configuration:
[permutation check page](qtl_mapping_betabinomial_pc_window_permutation.html).

# 2. Choosing k

The scan was run for k = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 15 phenotype PCs: all at 5, 20 and
50 kb, and k = 0, 1, 3 and 5 also at 100 and 200 kb. As in the paper, k is
chosen to **maximise discoveries**.

```{r ktable, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.8}
ws <- sort(unique(ST$window_kb)); ks <- sort(unique(ST$npcs))
hm <- merge(CJ(npcs = ks, window_kb = ws), ST[, .(npcs, window_kb, disc_q10, disc_q05)], by = c("npcs", "window_kb"), all.x = TRUE)
hm[, `:=`(w = factor(paste0(window_kb, " kb"), paste0(ws, " kb")), k = factor(npcs, rev(ks)),
          lab = fifelse(is.na(disc_q10), "not run", sprintf("%d\n(%d)", disc_q10, disc_q05)))]
hm[!is.na(disc_q10), best := disc_q10 == max(disc_q10), by = window_kb]
hm[, ink := fifelse(!is.na(disc_q10) & disc_q10 > mean(range(disc_q10, na.rm = TRUE)), "white", "grey15")]
ggplot(hm, aes(w, k)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = disc_q10), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = ink, fontface = fifelse(best %in% TRUE, "bold", "plain")), size = 3.4, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e8f0fb", high = "#1a4f8f", na.value = "grey92", name = "eSites (q < 0.10)") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  labs(x = "cis window", y = "phenotype PCs (k)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
```

eSites at q < 0.10, with q < 0.05 in brackets; the best k in each window is in bold.
k = 0, 1, 3 and 5 come from one run over all five windows, and k = 7, 10, 15 from the
first run (5-50 kb); the two runs agree exactly where they overlap.

```{r kbest}
ts <- sn[window_kb == min(ws), setNames(tested_sites, npcs)]
bk <- ST[, .SD[which.max(disc_q10)], by = window_kb]
stopifnot(all(bk$npcs %in% c(0, 1)))   # the text below says k = 0 or 1 gives the most eSites at every window
```

**Fewer PCs give more eSites.** k = 0 or k = 1 gives the most eSites at every window:
`r e(0, 5)` and `r e(1, 5)` at 5 kb against `r e(3, 5)` at k = 3, and `r e(0, 50)` and
`r e(1, 50)` at 50 kb against `r e(3, 50)`. Phenotype PCs therefore do not increase
power here.

k = 0 is tested on fewer sites than the other settings (`r fmt(ts[["0"]])` against
`r fmt(ts[["1"]])` at k = 1, at 5 kb). With no PCs the null model is intercept-only,
and at about a thousand shallow sites its dispersion estimate runs to the boundary
(no overdispersion); the optimiser then stops at its iteration limit and the fit is
discarded, although the best fit is simply the binomial one. Before switching, the
calibration of k = 0 and 1 is being checked (1 real + 5 genome-wide permutations, as
for k = 3).

```{r kplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.2}
pd <- ST[, .(k = factor(npcs), window_kb, eSites = disc_q10)]
ggplot(pd, aes(window_kb, eSites, colour = k)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = ws) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`0` = "#2a78d6", `1` = "#eb6834", `3` = "#1baf7a", `5` = "#eda100", `7` = "#e87ba4",
                                 `10` = "#008300", `15` = "#6250d6"), name = "phenotype PCs (k)") +
  labs(x = "cis window (kb, log scale)", y = "eSites (q < 0.10)") + th
```

Among k = 3 to 15, discoveries fall as k grows; k = 0 and 1 give the most at every window.

# 3. Choosing the cis window

## Where the strong associations are (the paper's approach)

To choose its window, the paper tested every SNP within 2 Mb of each peak and
looked at how far the strongly associated SNPs lie (their Fig. 1c). We did the
same: a nominal scan of every SNP within **+/-2 Mb** of each site at k = 3
(`r fmt(nrow(S))` SNP-site pairs with p < 1e-4), drawn with the paper's own plotting
choices.

```{r fig1c, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.6}
CUTS <- c(1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6); LAB <- c("p < 1e-4", "p < 1e-5", "p < 1e-6")
ec <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(CUTS), function(j) S[p_nominal < CUTS[j], .(absd, cutoff = LAB[j])]))[, cutoff := factor(cutoff, LAB)]
ggplot(ec, aes(absd, colour = cutoff)) + stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("black", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7"), LAB), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2e6, 2e5), labels = paste(seq(0, 2e6, 2e5) / 1000, "kb"), expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  labs(x = "distance from the pU site", y = "cumulative proportion of SNP-site pairs") + th +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = c(0.8, 0.3))
sh <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(CUTS), function(j) S[p_nominal < CUTS[j], .(cutoff = LAB[j], n = .N,
  w5 = mean(absd <= 5e3), w20 = mean(absd <= 2e4), w50 = mean(absd <= 5e4), w100 = mean(absd <= 1e5), w200 = mean(absd <= 2e5))]))
```

```{r shares}
knitr::kable(sh[, .(cutoff, pairs = fmt(n), `within 5 kb` = pct(w5), `within 50 kb` = pct(w50),
                    `within 100 kb` = pct(w100), `within 200 kb` = pct(w200))])
```

Most strongly associated SNPs lie within 100 kb of the site
(`r pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w100)` at p < 1e-6), which is the paper's criterion for its 100 kb
window. Few are within 5 kb (`r pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w5)`).

## The trade-off

```{r tradeoff}
knitr::kable(data.table(window = paste0(ws, " kb"), `eSites, k = 0` = sapply(ws, function(w) e(0, w)),
  `k = 1` = sapply(ws, function(w) e(1, w)), `k = 3` = sapply(ws, function(w) e(3, w)),
  `strong pairs within the window (p < 1e-6)` = c(pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w5), pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w20), pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w50),
                                                  pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w100), pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w200))))
```

eSites at q < 0.10 (all tested sites). The distance profile comes from the +/-2 Mb
scan at k = 3.

- **5 kb** gives the most eSites at every k (k = 1: `r e(1, 5)`; k = 3: `r e(3, 5)`): fewer
  SNPs per site means a lighter multiple-testing burden, and the strongest enrichment is
  close to the site.
- **100 kb** follows the paper's criterion and captures most strong associations,
  at the cost of fewer eSites (k = 1: `r e(1, 100)`; k = 3: `r e(3, 100)`). 200 kb gives fewer still (k = 3: `r e(3, 200)`) and adds few
  strong associations (`r pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w200)` within the window, against `r pct(sh[cutoff == "p < 1e-6"]$w100)` at 100 kb).

**Decision pending:** 5 kb or 100 kb.

# Data and scripts

- k x window scans: `qtl_betabinomial/pc_window_selection/` (k = 3-15, 5-50 kb) and
  `qtl_betabinomial/pc_window_selection_w200kb/` (k = 3, 5, 5-200 kb); scripts
  `47.scan_pc_window_selection.R`, `48.pc_window_selection_summary.R`,
  `50.selection_inheritedC_setaside.R`.
- +/-2 Mb nominal scan: `qtl_betabinomial/nominal_wide_window/`; scripts
  `56.scan_nominal_wide_window.R`, `57.window_distance_summary.R`, `59.paper_style_fig1c.R`.
- Related pages: [Stage 1 summary](stage1_phenotype_preparation.html),
  [permutation check](qtl_mapping_betabinomial_pc_window_permutation.html),
  [model](qtl_mapping_betabinomial_model.html).
